items.title: 13.10.2 Reaction with hot aqueous sodium hydroxide

blocks.text: With hot aqueous sodium hydroxide chlorine forms sodium chloride and sodium chlorate(V), NaClO3, another disproportionation: 3Cl2(g) + 6NaOH(aq) gives 5NaCl(aq) + NaClO3(aq) + 3H2O(l). Chlorine is 0 in Cl2, -1 in NaCl and +5 in NaClO3: it is oxidised from 0 to +5 in NaClO3 and reduced from 0 to -1 in NaCl. The reaction shows how temperature influences the products and the versatility of chlorine in redox reactions.
